summary: The repair was applied in a separate patched working copy: the redirect-auth rebuild step now strips the Authorization header unless scheme, case-folded hostname and effective port all match, with implicit default ports substituted when omitted; the netrc re-lookup below the branch is unchanged. Re-running the identical secure-to-plaintext redirect against the patched copy delivered the hop to the plaintext target with no Authorization header (final status 200), while the keep direction held: same-origin plaintext-to-plaintext and TLS-to-TLS redirects still carried the header, cross-host still stripped, a POST through a cross-scheme 307 preserved method and body while stripping credentials, a same-origin 308 kept both credential and body, and the netrc credential was re-attached for a cross-host hop exactly as before the repair. A 14-row predicate table matched the intended keep/strip table on every row after the repair, versus four hostname-only deviations before it (scheme-change and same-host port-change pairs).
next_hint: The repair closes the single-hop leak with positive and negative wire controls, and the predicate table matches design including explicit versus implicit default ports and case-folded hostnames. Two independent checks remain before export: the package's own redirect/auth test subset must stay green on the repaired copy (contract neutrality, compared against the vulnerable copy), and a three-hop chain driven by one session must not carry or re-attach the original credential at later hops. Both run on loopback with the existing fixture; no new permissions are needed.
